requirements.name: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
requirements.raw_text: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units

courses.title: English First Year Experience
courses.description: Introduces incoming English students to the department by helping connect them to CPP-specific resources such as student support services, curricular advising, career planning, library resources, student organizations, clubs, and affinity groups. Introduces the program’s learning outcomes to prepare students for success in the program.
courses.prerequisites: Declared English major.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Introduction to English Linguistics
courses.description: [GE 3B] The study of English as a science and a cultural phenomenon. Exploration of fundamental properties of English and of ways in which English differs from other languages. Topics include the sounds, word formation and meaning, syntax, history, and dialects of English.

courses.title: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.description: Fundamentals of studying literature. Exercises in reading practices, writing analytical papers, research, theory, and revision.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 205, ENG 207, ENG 208, ENG 211, ENG 212, ENG 213, ENG 217, ENG 218, ENG 2300 , ENG 2320 , ENG 2330 , ENG 2331 , ENG 2332 , ENG 2510 , ENG 2520 , ENG 2710 , or ENG 2720 .

courses.title: Literary Theory and Cultural Studies
courses.description: Analysis of the works of selected major literary critics. Application of theoretical principles in original critical essays.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 205, ENG 207, ENG 208, ENG 211, ENG 212, ENG 213, ENG 217, ENG 218, ENG 2300 , ENG 2320 , ENG 2330 , ENG 2331 , ENG 2332 , ENG 2510 , ENG 2520 , ENG 2710 , or ENG 2720 .

courses.title: Introduction to Rhetorical Theory
courses.description: Rhetorical analyses of literary, political, and scientific texts. Emphasis on how rhetorical design of texts appeals to readers.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Writing for the Professions
courses.description: Rhetorical principles of business and other professional writing. Extensive practice in writing letters, memos, reports, and other professional documents.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: The Grammar of Modern English
courses.description: Modern English syntax and morphology. Emphasis on Standard English. Discussion of grammatical variations in other social and regional dialects. Grammatical text analysis.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 214 or ENG 2200 .

courses.title: American Literature Since 1865
courses.description: [GE 3B] An introductory survey of American literature since the Civil War including authors (like Twain, Hurston, Ellison, Silko, or Pynchon), themes (like class, race, gender, or trauma), or aesthetic movements (like the Harlem Renaissance or the Beat Generation).
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Introduction to Multicultural Literature in the U.S.
courses.description: [GE 3B] Introduction to the role of ethnic and cultural identification in shaping literature by U.S. writers. May include but is not limited to writing by authors of African, Asian, Arabic, European, Hispanic, and/or Native American heritage.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: British Literature II
courses.description: [GE 3B] The study of major authors and their literary texts from the Romantic, Victorian, and Modern periods with attention to the historical and cultural contexts.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Literature II
courses.description: [GE 3B] Major themes such as the journey from Faith to Reason, the unconscious and irrational, or crises of morality, in selected literary masterpieces from western and non-western cultures, from the 11th century CE to the present with emphasis on historical contexts.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Introduction to U.S. Latino/a Literature
courses.description: [GE 3B] Introduction to works by and about Latino/as in English within a broader historical and cultural context. Study of the history of this umbrella category that includes many different national and hybrid identities with an eye toward the shared experiences of colonialism, migration, and racialization.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Literature and the African American Experience
courses.description: [GE 3B or 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2332 Uses an Ethnic Studies framework to look at African American literature within historical, cultural, social, political, and economic conditions in order to better understand contemporary racial politics, structural racism, and strategies of resistance. Topics may include the relationship between Neo-Slave Narratives and the Civil Rights Movement, the Black Arts Movement and the Black Power movement in the 1970s, or Afrofuturism and post-racial discourse in the present.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: The Bible as Literature
courses.description: [GE 3B] Selected texts from the Old and New Testaments featuring biblical writing in the King James version such as narrative, poetry, wisdom literature, synoptic gospels, and Pauline letters involving the study of types in typology and archetypes.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Introduction to Folklore
courses.description: [GE 3B] A survey of medieval to modern folk tales, with attention to oral conventions, text production and transmission, and to the formal similarities and geographic differences within the tradition.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Fantasy and the Fantastic
courses.description: [GE 3B] Fantasy as a literary genre. The history of fantasy and the nature of the fantastic. The significance of fantasy in human society and thought.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Science Fiction
courses.description: [GE 3B] Science fiction as a literary genre. The history of science fiction. The significance of science fiction in contemporary life and thought.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: War and Peace in Literature
courses.description: [GE 3B] Selected ancient and modern texts with themes of war and peace from various cultural traditions read comparatively with a focus on the sociocultural roots of violence and the cultivation of literary visions of nonviolence.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Women Writers
courses.description: [GE 3B] Selected readings in works of fiction, poetry, drama, and/or expository prose by women writers. Emphasis on the diversity of women’s writing and the contribution to literature by women authors.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
courses.description: The study of teaching English in international language settings, including EFL methodology, cultural issues, necessary skill sets, practical issues, with classroom teaching opportunities.

courses.title: Writing for the Web Activity
courses.description: Writing practicum for digital platforms. Working under the direction of the department webmaster, student writer/designers write and produce news stories and other content for departmental web site, blogs, and other web platforms.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 301 or ENG 3151 .

courses.title: Journal Publishing Activity
courses.description: Advertise, select manuscripts, produce, publish, and distribute CPP’s literary magazine, Harvest International .
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Work with faculty to define a collaborative research project, develop a methodology or theoretical framework, gather sources/data, and prepare results for presentation and/or publication.
courses.prerequisites: Junior Standing and Approval by the Undergraduate Research Coordinator.

courses.title: Internship Cooperative Education
courses.description: A practical on-the-job professional experience related to writing for the workplace that affords the student the opportunity to put into practice the knowledge and skills attained in coursework. Application forms available from the EFL Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior Standing and Internship Coordinator Approval.

courses.title: Careers for English Majors
courses.description: Research career options/paths related to disciplines in English Studies and options in the major. Develop online job search presence and job application materials. Network in organizations/industries of interest.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Sub-area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Senior Symposium
courses.description: Students engage in intensive study of a major author to integrate and demonstrate mastery of core disciplinary areas: literature, literary theory, linguistics, and rhetoric. Emphasis on close reading, theoretical application, advanced writing, and reflective analysis. Designed to synthesize knowledge and skills developed throughout the English program. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Senior standing, and two 4000-level English courses.

courses.title: Literature, Power, and Politics
courses.description: Analysis of literary texts concerned with the development and implementation of political policies that affect various communities. Topics may include U.S. immigration laws and policies, nationalism/postnationalism, globality, neoliberalism, displacement, exile, and diaspora formation as reflected in literature.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 205, ENG 207, ENG 208, ENG 211, ENG 212, ENG 213, ENG 217, ENG 218, ENG 2300 , ENG 2320 , ENG 2330 , ENG 2331 , ENG 2332 , ENG 2510 , ENG 2520 , ENG 2710 , or ENG 2720 .

courses.title: American Poetic Traditions
courses.description: Critical analysis of American poetry from colonial era to the present day. Poets such as Bradstreet, Wheatley, Bryant, Longfellow, Poe, Whitman, Dickinson, Dunbar, Eliot, Pound, Bishop, Frost, McKay, Hughes, Rich, Baraka, Ginsberg, and Collins.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Shakespeare before 1600
courses.description: [GE 3C] Selected plays from the first half of Shakespeare’s career, focusing primarily on the comedies and histories, but with some exploration of the early tragedies as well.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: British Drama to 1890
courses.description: Explores the development English Drama from the medieval mystery and morality plays to the late nineteenth century, with an emphasis on non-Shakespearean drama and on the transformation from text to performance in the different theaters.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Novel in English
courses.description: Developments and directions in the novel in the Anglophone world from its origins to the contemporary with an emphasis determined by the instructor. Thematic concerns and technical developments in fiction by English language authors representing diverse backgrounds and approaches as well as colonial and postcolonial concerns.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Modern Drama
courses.description: Explores the development of Continental, British and American drama from the rise of Naturalism through Modern and Postmodern periods. Employs both literary and theatrical approaches to this drama, with a focus on the transformation from text to performance.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Myth as Literature
courses.description: Survey of classical mythologies, such as Roman and/or Norse. Emphasis on the literary qualities of myths, on their authors, and on the myths as the basis for later literature.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Epic
courses.description: Survey of classical, medieval, and modern epics, with attention to conventions of the genre and the distinctions between primary and secondary epics.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Film as Literary Genre
courses.description: Uses media studies and genre theory to analyze the sociocultural work of films. Looking at the aesthetic decisions of filmmakers, students consider how visual narratives are constructed and the way those decisions shape our view of the world. Topics may include adaptation, performance studies, the gaze, fandoms, inequity in the film industry, and/or the development of cinematic universes.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013 , or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Graphic Novels and Visual Aesthetics
courses.description: Looking at the historical development of the various “sequential arts” alongside critical comics studies and genre theory, students consider the impact of comics and graphic novels on how readers experience the world. Topics may include memoir and serialization, materiality and adaptation, or fandom and cosplay.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013 , or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Multicultural Literature in the U.S.
courses.description: Expansion on the definition of U.S. literature through the study of Latino, Native American, African American, Asian and Pacific American, and ethnically specific Euro-American literary works, their authors, and their cultural contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013 , or ENG 3110 . Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Hemispheric American Literature
courses.description: Literary texts from the Western Hemisphere read with particular attention to themes of history, the past and its uses, nationalism and transnationalism, and the interconnectivity of literatures written in the Americas.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: African American Literature
courses.description: Exploration of African American literary works, authors, and cultural contexts. Potential topics include slave narratives and tales of resistance, the Harlem Renaissance and the Black Arts Movement, civil rights and the Prison-Industrial Complex.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Native American Literature
courses.description: Native American literary texts reflective of how Native American writers represent their cultural histories and thought systems. Topics such as storytelling and orality; languages and the written word; identity and sovereignty.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Colonial and Postcolonial Literature
courses.description: Literatures of Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, Latin America, and/or the Middle East, including implications for non-white writers in the U.S. Topics include colonialism, racism, tourism, nationhood, and/or cultural identity. Writers such as Memmi, Zobel, Kincaid, Desai, Ousmane, Fuentes, and/or Mishima.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Literature of Exile
courses.description: Literature of incarceration or displacement produced by writers who have experienced exile and/or live outside of their homelands. Emphasis on the influence of exile on national literature and on transnational literary movements. Writers such as Levi, Hoffman, Sebbar, and/or Ninh.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Chinese Civilization and Culture
courses.description: [GE 3C] Comprehensive study of Chinese civilizational heritage and cultural traditions from cross-cultural and interdisciplinary perspectives. Reading and discussion focus on Chinese philosophy, literature, art, and sciences to achieve an in-depth synthetic understanding of China’s past and present. The course is taught in English.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Intersectionality and Literature
courses.description: The study of fiction, poetry, drama, and nonfiction in which categories of difference including race, gender, sexuality, ability, and class are present as major themes, strategies, or narrative effects.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Technologies of Writing
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: [GE 3C] A multimodal introduction to material processes of writing, analysis, and rhetoric including: historical composition practices such as manuscript and letterpress; textile crafts such as needlecraft and scrapbooking; and digital making such as textual editing, multimodal storytelling, and design.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: 19th C. American Literature
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Critical analysis of literature written in and about North America during the nineteenth century. Writers such as Sedgwick, Irving, Poe, Hawthorne, Douglass, Fern, Melville, Stowe, Dickinson, Whitman, Jacobs, Alcott, Twain, and Dunbar.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Chaucer
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Introduction to Middle English language and culture, followed by a close reading of Chaucer’s magnum opus, The Canterbury Tales, and other works.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Literature of the English Civil War
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: The texts of Milton and his contemporaries as understood within the context of literary theory, literary history, politics, and cultural studies, and their influence on Anglophone literature and culture. Emphasis on critical reading, thinking, and discussion.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Enlightenment
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: The Enlightenment features study in major authors (e.g. Behn, Dryden, Swift, Pope, Gay, and Johnson among others), various genres, historical contexts, and thematic issues such as, but not limited to: empire, colonialism, empiricism, satire, and aesthetics.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: British Romanticism
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: How do history and politics shape poetic production, especially the French Revolution? What were the industrial and environmental implications? This seminar will consider the historical-political context for English Romanticism and offer a sample of the major work: Romantic lyrics, closet drama, fragment, epic, prose, and criticism.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: British Victorian Age
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: British Victorian Age features representative work from major authors through these genres: lyric poetry (e.g., sonnet, elegy, dramatic monologue), drama, novel, and criticism. The Victorian era (1837-1901) addresses issues about: Marriage, the Woman Question, Darwinism, Industrial Revolution, and Cultural Identity among other topics.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: The Novel in the Modern World
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: The twentieth-century novel outside the U.S. and Great Britain, with attention to philosophical and aesthetic responses to the changing world. Emphasis on individuals’ struggles to define their sense of identity and freedom. Writers such as Camus, Kundera, Kincaid, and/or Duong.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Viewing Words; Reading Pictures
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: A comparative study of inter-artistic relations in western and nonwestern literature and art. Focused reading of major inter-artistic theories facilitates an in-depth analysis of selected works of thematic, cultural, and periodic diversity from both arts.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Contemporary Literature
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Advanced study of literature written in the last 25 years. The course engages with literature whose content is immediate and present in our lives and considers how art’s imagined present crystallizes as literary history.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013 , or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Modernism and Postmodernism
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: [GE 3C] Advanced study in the 20th/21st century literary and cultural movements of modernism and postmodernism, manifesting in disciplines of literature (Pynchon, Rushdie), film (Fight Club, Vertigo), art (Picasso and Banksy), television (Community), history, philosophy, and/or politics.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: British Renaissance
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: English poets from 1500 to 1660, including Wyatt, Sidney, Spenser, Marlowe, Shakespeare, Wroth, Lanyer, Jonson, Donne, Herbert, Marvell and others.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 312 or ENG 3000 ; and ENG 350, ENG 355, ENG 3010 , ENG 3011 , ENG 3012 , ENG 3013, or ENG 3110 .

courses.title: Mexican Literature
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Examination of key themes, ideas, trends and authors in Mexican and Chicano literature through the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. All readings in Spanish.
courses.prerequisites: SPN 2112 or SPN 2120 .

courses.title: Modern and Vanguard Poetry
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Transatlantic study of literary modernity in the Hispanic world from 1890 to 1990, including modernism and the vanguards, with particular attention to poetry. Course conducted in Spanish.
courses.prerequisites: SPN 2112 or SPN 2120 .

courses.title: Hispanic Literature in the Age of Global Encounters
courses.requirement: Additional courses from Genre, Decentered Canons, and below: 6 units
courses.description: Consideration of varying accounts of the formation and transformation of Spanish letters across the geographical boundaries of the Spanish empire (sixteenth-century Rome and sixteenth-century Mexico). The course will also consider the multifarious readings that the Spanish Empire had on the verge of Modernity and how Spanish practices influenced the literature of the British empire. Corequisite(s): SPN 2112 or SPN 2120 .

courses.title: The History of the English Language
courses.description: Principles of historical language change as an aid to understanding present-day pronunciation, spelling, word formation, grammar, and usage in English. Social and cultural influences on the language.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 214 or ENG 2200 .

courses.title: Sociolinguistics
courses.description: [GE 4C] The study of language use in society and of mutual influences of society and language. Focus on regional and social dialectology, language ideology, language and social categories (gender, ethnicity, social class).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Analysis of Conversation
courses.description: Study of sequences of spoken utterances. Emphasis on linguistic and interactional characteristics of conversation, with comparisons of conversational practices across cultures
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing, senior standing, or ENG 2200 .

courses.title: Applied Pragmatics
courses.description: Study of relationship between linguistic forms and their uses within a context. Focus on forms involved in deixis, speech acts, implicature, and politeness theory. Emphasis on practical applications in the business world and the language classroom.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing, senior standing, or completion of GE Area 1A/A2; and ENG 2200 or ENG 214.

courses.title: Genre Fiction
courses.description: Study of novels and short stories written in popular genres such as science fiction, fantasy, crime, suspense, horror, and romance. Historical, critical and creative writing approaches.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.description: The fundamentals of creative writing. Exercises in plotting, characterization, dialogue, description, narration, and point of view. Readings; analysis of stories and exercises.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Creative Non-Fiction
courses.description: Fundamentals of writing creative non-fiction. Exercises in structural organization, characterization, dialogue, point of view and focalization, argumentation. Revision of drafts toward submission for publication.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Creative Writing: Poetry
courses.description: The fundamentals of poetry writing. Exercises in poetic forms, genres, and traditions. Readings; analysis of poems and exercises.
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Creative Writing: World-Building
courses.description: A creative writing workshop on fictional world-building. Through literary analysis and collaborative tabletop roleplaying, students will design a world-its languages, histories, artifacts, cultures-for fiction, gameplay, and publication.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 3000 or ENG 312, and junior standing.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
